svg.title: CPU vs GPU memory hierarchy pyramids
svg.desc: Two side-by-side pyramids, CPU and GPU, each with four layers — registers, then L1/L2/L3 cache vs SMEM+L1/L2 cache, then DRAM vs HBM — labelled with capacity, bandwidth, and latency. The GPU pyramid is wider at every level, showing far higher absolute bandwidth, but an annotation explains that the compute-to-bandwidth ratio (the ridge point) is actually worse on the GPU, not better.

text.font-family: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Memory hierarchy: same shape, shifted numbers, worse ratio

svg.text: even faster. The ratio that matters is FLOP/byte, which sets the ridge (≈295 on an H100): a

svg.text: GPU's compute-to-bandwidth ratio is worse than a CPU's, which is why inference starves for bytes.
